Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherMed Devices Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Thornton, CEO; Elena Vasquez, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Thornton.

Alex Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AetherMed Devices delivered strong results this quarter, driven by increasing adoption of our innovative medical devices and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance: competitive dynamics and market share trends; R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress; FDA approvals and CE marks obtained; hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates; and overall performance highlights and key achievements.

Elena will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with competitive dynamics and market share trends, which continue to underscore the strength of our portfolio across key medical device segments. As you know, the global medical devices market is projected to exceed $650 billion by 2028, growing at a solid 5.2% CAGR, driven by aging demographics, rising procedure volumes, and the shift toward value-based care. Within this landscape, we've methodically expanded our leadership positions, gaining approximately 120 basis points of share year-over-year in our core markets, bringing our blended market share to 14.2% globally—up from 13.1% last year.

Let me break this down by our primary franchises, starting with orthopedics, which represents about 35% of our revenue. Here, we're the clear number two player behind Stryker, holding a robust 22% U.S. market share in hips and knees, per the latest NPM data through Q3. We've clawed back 80 basis points from Zimmer Biomet and Smith+Nephew through our next-gen Cementless Triad Hip System, which has seen 28% procedure share adoption among high-volume surgeons—well ahead of the category average of 18%. Pricing remains disciplined, with ASPs up 4% sequentially, supported by favorable reimbursement under the CMS IPPS updates. Internationally, we're accelerating in APAC, where we've grown share to 12% in Japan and China combined, up from 9% a year ago, fueled by our JTEKT partnership for localized manufacturing and navigating NMPA approvals ahead of peers.

Shifting to cardiovascular, our largest segment at 42% of revenue, the competitive intensity is high with Medtronic and Boston Scientific dominating. Nonetheless, we've maintained our 18.5% share in structural heart—our Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) platform now commands 26% U.S. procedure share, gaining 150 basis points on Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 Ultra. This momentum stems from our EvoQ TAVR device's lower paravalvular leak rates (under 2% in our PROPEL registry data versus industry 5-7%) and expanded indications into low-risk patients, aligning with the pivotal PARTNER 3 trial outcomes. In rhythm management, our Micra leadless pacemaker has driven a 10% share gain to 22% globally, outpacing Abbott's Aveir due to our VR2+ model's 15% smaller footprint and MR-conditional labeling. Europe remains a bright spot, with 16% share growth in TAVR post-CE Mark renewals, though headwinds from Germany's DRG reimbursement caps have tempered ASPs by 2%.

In robotics and minimally invasive, a high-growth area now at 15% of our mix, we're challenging Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci monopoly head-on. Our Orion Xi dual-console system has captured 11% U.S. share in soft-tissue procedures within 18 months of launch—impressive given Intuitive's 85%+ incumbency. Adoption is accelerating, with over 450 systems placed and utilization rates hitting 85% (versus da Vinci's 78% peer average), thanks to our AI-driven EndoSense tissue feedback and single-use FlexiArm instruments, which reduce OR setup time by 22%. Procedurally, we're up 35% YoY in gyn and urology volumes. Emerging markets like India and Brazil offer upside, where we've inked distribution deals adding $50 million in pipeline TAM.

Regional dynamics are pivotal. In the U.S., which drives 55% of our revenue, we're resilient amid hospital consolidation—gaining share from smaller players like CONMED in endoscopy via our 4K Vizor scopes. Procedure volumes are rebounding to 98% of pre-COVID levels per Definitive Healthcare, boosting our mix. EMEA contributes 25%, with flat share at 13% due to U.K. NHS backlogs, but we're optimistic on our neurostimulation franchise overtaking Nevro's HF10 in chronic pain, where we've hit 19% share on Senza-like outcomes at lower cost. APAC, at 15% of revenue, is our fastest grower at 22% YoY, with China share doubling to 8% on our domestic robotic production ramp to sidestep U.S. tariffs and local content rules.

Strategically, these trends reflect our three-pillar approach: (1) innovation velocity, with $1.2 billion in R&D yielding 12 FDA approvals YTD and 25+ IDE studies; (2) M&A discipline, like our $800 million acquisition of NeuroVive for neuromodulation IP, adding 200 bps to neuro share; and (3) commercial excellence, including our SurgeonSync digital platform, which has lifted same-surgeon retention by 15% through predictive analytics on implant utilization. Risks include supply chain fragility—titanium pricing up 12% from Ukraine impacts—and biosimilar erosion in cardiology stents, but our vertical integration mitigates 70% of this.

Looking forward, we expect to gain another 100-150 basis points in 2024, targeting 15.5% blended share, with robotics and structural heart as key drivers. Our conviction is high: we're not just participating in the market; we're reshaping it through superior clinical evidence and surgeon partnerships.

Now, let's talk about R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. Innovation is the lifeblood of the medical devices industry, especially in cardiology and vascular interventions where we're navigating a rapidly evolving landscape marked by aging demographics, the shift to value-based care, and accelerating demand for minimally invasive and digital-enabled therapies. We're pleased to report that our disciplined approach to R&D continues to deliver strong momentum, positioning us for sustained growth amid competitive pressures from peers like Boston Scientific, Medtronic, and Abbott Laboratories.

Let me start with the numbers. In the third quarter, we invested $285 million in research and development, representing 14.2% of our total revenue—up from 12.8% in Q3 of last year and slightly above our long-term target range of 13-15%. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year R&D growth, totaling $850 million year-to-date, a 17% increase. For context, this outpaces the industry average of around 11-12% of sales, as reported in recent Deloitte medtech benchmarking data, and reflects our strategic overweight in high-ROI areas like next-generation structural heart devices and AI-augmented imaging. We funded this through robust free cash flow generation—$420 million in Q3 alone—and selective capital raises, maintaining a healthy R&D-to-revenue ratio while preserving our investment-grade balance sheet.

Turning to pipeline progress, our portfolio spans over 45 active programs across preclinical, clinical, and regulatory stages, with a weighted average time-to-market of 24 months—down from 30 months two years ago, thanks to streamlined internal processes and external partnerships. Let me highlight key advancements by therapeutic area.

In structural heart, our flagship TC-7 transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) system achieved a major milestone last month with positive 12-month data from the pivotal TRILOGY trial. Enrollment completed ahead of schedule at 450 patients across 35 global sites, showing 95% technical success, 2.1% 30-day mortality—competitive with Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien platform—and sustained hemodynamic improvements with a mean mitral valve gradient of 4.2 mmHg at one year. We're on track to submit our PMA to the FDA in Q1 2025, with a potential U.S. launch in H2 2026, representing a $1.2 billion peak sales opportunity in the $8 billion-plus TMVR market growing at 22% CAGR per Grand View Research.

Complementing this, our next-gen left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) device, PulseGuard LA, advanced to full enrollment in its U.S. IDE study with 1,200 patients. Early interim analysis demonstrated a 28% reduction in procedure time versus the Watchman FLX—now the market leader—and a leak rate under 1%, addressing a key pain point in this $2.5 billion segment. CE Mark under MDR was granted in July, enabling a controlled EU launch in Q4 this year via our distribution agreement with Terumo Europe, where we're targeting 15% share in Germany and France within three years.

Shifting to electrophysiology, we're making waves in pulsed-field ablation (PFA), the hottest trend since cryoballoon tech disrupted thermal RF. Our FARAPULSE 2.0 system, building on our initial FARAPULSE platform which captured 18% U.S. market share in Q3, completed first-in-human cases in our ADVENT-2 trial last week. Featuring a next-gen multi-array catheter with integrated mapping, it achieved 99% pulmonary vein isolation in under 20 minutes, with zero esophageal injuries in preclinical swine models. Regulatory submission to the FDA is slated for mid-2025, positioning us to challenge Medtronic's Affera portfolio in a market projected to hit $5 billion by 2028, driven by the MANIFEST-PF registry data underscoring PFA's safety profile.

On the digital health front, where we're allocating 22% of our R&D budget—up from 15% last year—our AI-powered CardioAI platform hit an inflection point. Integrated with our imaging suites, it now uses convolutional neural networks trained on 50,000+ anonymized angiograms to predict stent restenosis risk with 92% accuracy, outperforming manual assessments per our validation study published in JACC: Cardiovascular Interventions. We've partnered with GE Healthcare for cloud deployment, and early adopter sites in the U.S. Veterans Health Administration reported a 35% reduction in unnecessary follow-ups. Full FDA 510(k) clearance is expected Q4 2024, unlocking $300 million in recurring SaaS revenue by 2027 as telecardiology booms post-COVID.

Regionally, our pipeline is diversified to mitigate regulatory headwinds. In the U.S., FDA feedback has been constructive, with breakthrough device designation on three assets—TC-7, PulseGuard, and CardioAI—accelerating review by six months on average. Europe remains a launchpad, with MDR compliance now complete for 80% of our EU portfolio, though Class III delays pushed two programs back by three months; we're countering this with localized trials in the Nordics. In Asia-Pacific, our China NMPA approval for the legacy FARAPULSE platform drove $45 million in Q3 sales, up 40% YoY, and we're investing $50 million in a Shanghai R&D hub to localize our TMVR for the 300 million hypertension patients there. Japan PMDA submission for PulseGuard is underway, tapping into a $1 billion EP market underserved by domestic players like Johnson & Johnson's Biosense Webster.

Strategically, we're focusing on three pillars: (1) platform innovation to drive margin expansion—our bioresorbable polymer tech in next-gen stents reduced chronic inflammation by 40% in bench tests, aiming for 75% gross margins at scale versus 65% industry norm; (2) ecosystem partnerships, including our $200 million co-development deal with Siemens Healthineers for hybrid OR robotics, mirroring Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci model but tailored for endovascular procedures; and (3) M&A adjacency, with two tuck-in acquisitions YTD totaling $150 million for neuromodulation IP, bolstering our pipeline against competitors like Nevro.

Looking ahead, we expect R&D spend to rise to $1.1 billion for FY2024, or 14.5% of guidance revenue, fueling five major launches in 2025-2026 that could add $2.5 billion in incremental sales by 2028. Risks remain—clinical trial delays, pricing pressures under the CMS APC framework, and supply chain volatility for rare earths in our PFA catheters—but our 18-month cash runway and 25% pipeline success rate (versus industry 15%) give us conviction.

We're executing at pace, delivering therapies that save lives and bend the cost curve.

Moving on to FDA approvals and CE marks obtained, which underscore the strength of our R&D engine and positions us for accelerated revenue growth across our core franchises in cardiovascular interventions, neuromodulation, and minimally invasive robotics. As many of you know, the medical devices sector has faced headwinds from heightened FDA scrutiny under the latest PMA guidances and the EU's stringent MDR transition, now fully enforced post-2023 deadlines. Despite this, we've delivered a record haul of approvals, outpacing peers like Abbott Laboratories and Medtronic in submission-to-clearance timelines.

Let me break this down by key milestones, their commercial implications, and our strategic outlook.

FDA Approvals: A Banner Quarter with Breakthrough Momentum.

We secured three FDA approvals in Q3, including our first-ever PMA for the VascuFlow XT bioresorbable drug-eluting stent system, building on our 510(k)-cleared VascuFlow platform that's already captured 12% U.S. market share in peripheral artery disease (PAD) interventions. This PMA was granted under the Breakthrough Devices Program, shaving six months off the typical 18-24 month review cycle—our pivotal IDE trial met all primary endpoints with a 92% target lesion revascularization (TLR) freedom rate at 12 months, versus 85% for the predicate device comparator.

Complementing this, we received 510(k) clearance for two next-gen products: The NeuroPulse Gen3 RF ablation catheter for atrial fibrillation (AFib), featuring AI-driven lesion mapping that reduces procedure times by 28% per our benchtop and first-in-human data. This expands our label to include high-risk paroxysmal AFib patients, tapping into a $4.2B U.S. market growing at 9% CAGR per iData Research. The RoboAssist Pro endoscopic navigation system, a modular add-on to our existing da Vinci-competitive platform, cleared for colorectal and thoracic procedures. Early adopter feedback from our limited release shows a 35% reduction in operative complications, aligning with industry trends toward single-port robotics amid Boston Scientific's launch of the Ion platform.

Financially, these approvals are game-changers. We project $285 million in incremental U.S. revenue over FY2025-2027 from VascuFlow XT alone, with gross margins expanding to 72%—up 4 points from our legacy stents—thanks to scaled manufacturing at our Galway, Ireland facility. Overall, FDA approvals now cover 85% of our $2.1B U.S. revenue base, with Q4 launches driving 15-20% YoY growth in our CV segment, outstripping the 7% industry average per Evaluate MedTech forecasts.

CE Marks: MDR Compliance Unlocks EU Growth Engine.

On the international front, we achieved four CE marks under the Medical Device Regulation (MDR), a feat amid ongoing notified body bottlenecks—only 45% of legacy devices have recertified per Team-NB data. Our notified body, BSI, audited our quality systems flawlessly, reflecting investments in post-market surveillance (PMS) and clinical evaluation reports (CERs) compliant with MDCG 2024-1 guidelines.

Highlights include: Full MDR CE Mark for VascuFlow XT, enabling immediate EU commercialization in our highest-volume PAD indication. This is critical as EU PAD procedures grew 11% YoY in 2023, per Eurostat, yet reimbursement hurdles have slowed adoption. CE Mark for NeuroPulse Gen3, with expanded indications for persistent AFib, positioning us against Biosense Webster's CARTO ecosystem. Recertification of our OrthoFlex dynamic spinal implant and initial CE for EchoGuide AI ultrasound probe, which integrates real-time 3D imaging with 98% accuracy in vessel segmentation—vital for our structural heart pipeline.

Regionally, these open doors to EMEA revenue acceleration: EU5 direct markets now project $180M in FY2025 uplift, a 25% increase, while our distributor network in DACH (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) ramps to 40% attach rates on existing accounts. In Asia-Pacific, we're leveraging these for NMPA filings—pre-submission alignment yielded fast-track status for VascuFlow XT in China, targeting Q1 2025 approval amid a 14% CAGR market per Frost & Sullivan.

Technical Initiatives and Pipeline Synergies.

These wins stem from our $450M R&D spend (22% of revenue), focused on platform technologies like our proprietary nano-elution polymer for stents (reducing restenosis by 40% in preclinicals) and ML-optimized neuromodulation algorithms, trained on 50,000+ patient datasets. We've derisked 12 IDE submissions via the FDA's Q-Submission program, with 70% acceptance rates—double the industry norm.

Strategically, we're prioritizing indication expansions (e.g., VascuFlow XT's upcoming coronary pivot) and M&A bolt-ons, like our recent tuck-in of a Danish robotics startup mirroring Intuitive Surgical's playbook. Competitively, this vaults us ahead: our total addressable market penetration rises to 18% in CV devices, pressuring incumbents like Cook Medical in peripherals.

Forward-Looking Risks and Opportunities.

Of course, regulatory isn't risk-free—PMS data collection under EU IVDR/MDR could pressure margins short-term, and FDA's 2024 digital health transparency rules demand ongoing AI validation. But with a $1.2B cash position and 3.2x net debt/EBITDA, we're funding seven more submissions by YE2024.

In summary, these FDA and CE milestones validate our innovation moat, fueling mid-teens organic growth through the cycle.

Next, hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates—a key leading indicator for our procedural growth and recurring revenue streams in the Medical Devices space. As you know, adoption here refers to the percentage of our target accounts actively utilizing our capital equipment and consumables portfolio, including our flagship NeuroNav robotic navigation system, OrthoFlex modular implants, and CardioGuide ablation catheters. We're tracking this across our installed base of over 2,800 systems globally, with a focus on procedure mix, utilization rates, and penetration in high-volume ortho, spine, neuro, and structural heart segments.

Let me start with the headline numbers for Q3. Overall adoption across hospitals and ASCs reached 68% on a weighted average basis, up 12% year-over-year and 4% sequentially from Q2. This marks our 11th straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth, driven by a rebound in elective procedures now at 98% of pre-COVID volumes per our Symphony Health claims data. Breaking it down:

Hospital adoption: We hit 72% penetration in our top 500 U.S. integrated delivery networks (IDNs) and equivalent global hospital systems, up from 62% a year ago. This is fueled by our "Fleet Optimization Program," where we've deployed AI-driven analytics to boost case utilization from 18 to 24 procedures per system per month—a 33% lift. In ortho and spine, our OrthoFlex system's hospital attach rate for revision surgeries now exceeds 45%, outpacing competitors like Stryker's Mako by 8 points in head-to-head benchmarks from our Q3 user surveys.

ASC adoption: This is the real growth story, accelerating to 52% penetration across our 1,200 targeted ASCs, a robust 28% YoY increase. ASCs now represent 22% of our total procedure volume, up from 15% last year, aligning with the broader industry shift where outpatient ortho and pain management cases have surged 35% per MGMA data. Our CardioGuide catheter, optimized for same-day discharge electrophysiology procedures, saw ASC uptake jump to 61%, benefiting from streamlined FDA 510(k) clearances for low-acuity indications.

Trend-wise, we're seeing a clear bifurcation: hospitals remain our cash cow for high-complexity cases like robotic-assisted total joint replacements, but ASCs are cannibalizing lower-acuity volumes at a 15-20% CAGR through 2027, per our internal models and Grand View Research forecasts. Utilization rates are key here—our systems averaged 22.4 cases per month in Q3, with ASCs punching above their weight at 19.2 cases despite smaller OR footprints, thanks to our single-use FlexiArm consumables that reduce turnover time by 22% versus legacy disposables from Medtronic or Boston Scientific.

On the technical initiatives front, we've rolled out version 3.2 of our NeuroNav software, incorporating machine learning for real-time intraoperative imaging fusion. This has driven a 17% adoption bump in neuro-oncology procedures, with early adopters like Mayo Clinic reporting 15% OR efficiency gains. We've also expanded our Virtual Training Academy, delivering 4,500 surgeon certifications YTD—up 40% YoY—which correlates directly to a 25% faster ramp in new site adoption post-install. Capital sales reflected this, with 185 systems placed in Q3, 42% to ASCs, at an ASP of $1.8 million.

Regionally, the U.S. leads with 75% hospital and 58% ASC adoption, propelled by favorable CMS reimbursement under the 2024 OPPS final rule, which boosted APC payments for robotic ortho by 4.2%. Medicare Advantage penetration in ASCs hit 35% of our mix, underscoring value-based care tailwinds. Europe lagged slightly at 61% hospital adoption due to protracted tender cycles in Germany and the UK—think NHS procurement delays—but we're up 18% YoY post-CE Mark for our next-gen ablation tech, with strong traction in private chains like Ramsay Health Care. APAC is our fastest grower at 32% YoY, reaching 45% adoption; China's NMPA approval for OrthoFlex in July unlocked 120-bed hospital deals in Shanghai and Guangdong, while India's ASC boom—up 40% procedure volumes per IQVIA—positions us for 15% market share in minimally invasive spine by FY25.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on three levers: (1) ASC-centric product roadmap, with our upcoming FlexPort hub launching Q1 '25 to integrate multi-device workflows, targeting 65% ASC penetration; (2) surgeon economic incentives via our Outcomes360 rebate program, tying 10-15% of consumable revenue to quality metrics like length-of-stay reductions; and (3) M&A adjacency, as evidenced by our tuck-in acquisition of Ascend Robotics last month, adding IP for ASC-optimized arms to compete head-on with Intuitive Surgical's Ion platform in peripheral procedures.

Looking forward, we guide Q4 adoption to 71-73%, implying $285-295 million in consumables revenue at the midpoint, with ASC contribution growing to 25% of mix. Risks include supply chain headwinds on titanium alloys, now mitigated to <2% impact via dual-sourcing, and potential reimbursement cliffs under the SITE Act proposals. But with our 85% customer retention and net promoter score of 72, we're well-positioned to capture share in a $28 billion addressable market growing at 7.5% CAGR.

Finally, overall performance highlights and key achievements, which underscore the strength of our diversified portfolio in cardiovascular, orthopedic, and neuromodulation devices amid a resilient medical devices market valued at over $500 billion globally.

Starting with the top line: We delivered record Q3 revenue of $935 million, up 18% year-over-year and 5% on an organic basis, surpassing our guidance midpoint and consensus estimates by 3%. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, driven by a 22% surge in procedure-based revenues—reflecting robust hospital procedure volumes recovering to 95% of pre-pandemic levels—and a 12% increase in our capital equipment installed base, now exceeding 45,000 systems worldwide. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.55, a 25% improvement YoY, with margins expanding 210 basis points to 32.5% on the back of operating leverage, favorable mix shift toward high-margin consumables, and disciplined pricing amid stable Average Selling Prices, or ASPs, averaging $12,500 for our premium robotic-assisted surgery platforms.

Diving into segment performance, our Cardiovascular franchise—powered by our next-gen drug-eluting stents like the AetherFlex™ platform and TAVR valves akin to those from Edwards Lifesciences—grew 24% to $405 million, capturing 2.2 points of U.S. market share to reach 18% overall. This was fueled by a 15% increase in U.S. TAVR procedures, bolstered by expanded Medicare reimbursements under the CY2024 OPPS final rule, and our recent FDA PMA approval for the AetherFlex Ultra, which features bioresorbable scaffolds reducing restenosis rates by 35% in our pivotal TRIUMPH trial with over 2,500 patients.

In Orthopedics, revenues climbed 16% to $280 million, led by our 3D-printed implants and robotic navigation systems, which saw a 28% uptick in knee and hip replacement volumes. Our OrthoGuide™ robot, competitive with Stryker's Mako, now boasts an installed base of 8,200 units, generating $190 million in recurring revenue from procedure kits with attach rates exceeding 95%. Key here was our strategic partnership with Zimmer Biomet to co-develop AI-enhanced preoperative planning software, accelerating our penetration in the $15 billion global robotics orthopedics market.

Neuromodulation rounded out at $250 million, up 12%, with our RejuvaStim™ DBS systems for Parkinson's—similar to Medtronic's offerings—benefiting from a 19% procedure growth in Europe following CE Mark expansion into deep brain stimulation for epilepsy. Overall, our R&D investment hit 11.5% of revenue, or $108 million, funding 14 new product launches and 22 clinical trials, including Phase III data on our wearable cardiac monitors integrating AI algorithms that predict arrhythmias with 92% accuracy, rivaling Abbott's Confirm Rx.

Regionally, the U.S. contributed 52% of revenues, growing 21% on strong elective procedure rebound and our 510(k) clearances for seven new devices. EMEA delivered 28% growth to $300 million, navigating headwinds from the EU MDR transition—where we've achieved 95% portfolio compliance ahead of peers—while APAC surged 35% to $170 million, driven by a landmark distribution deal in China for our TAVR portfolio, tapping into a market projected to hit $4 billion by 2028 per Grand View Research. Emerging markets like LATAM and India added 14% growth, with our low-cost orthopedic kits gaining traction amid rising middle-class healthcare spend.

Strategically, these results validate our 'Innovation-First' roadmap: We've divested non-core diagnostics assets for $150 million to fund bolt-on M&A, including the $320 million acquisition of NeuroPulse Tech, bolstering our neuromodulation pipeline with closed-loop stimulation tech. Supply chain resilience remains a focus post-semiconductor shortages, with 85% localization in our new Singapore and Mexico facilities reducing lead times by 40%. Sustainability-wise, 65% of our devices now incorporate recycled materials, aligning with ESG mandates and positioning us for green procurement contracts.

Looking ahead, we're raising full-year guidance: Revenue growth to 16-18% organic, adjusted EPS to $6.10-$6.30, with Q4 procedure growth expected at 20%+. These achievements not only de-risk our growth but position AetherMed to outpace the 6-8% industry CAGR through 2030, capitalizing on megatrends like aging demographics, minimally invasive shifts, and digital therapeutics.

I will now turn the call over to Elena for a review of our financial results.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter, capped by record Q3 revenue of approximately $2 billion, up 18% year-over-year on an organic basis. This growth was broad-based across segments, with cardiovascular up 24%, orthopedics 16%, robotics and minimally invasive 35%, and neuromodulation 12%, aligning with the share gains and adoption trends Alex detailed.

Gross profit expanded to $1.4 billion, or 70% of revenue, up 320 basis points year-over-year, driven by higher-margin consumables now 62% of mix, manufacturing efficiencies at our Ireland and Singapore sites, and favorable forex. Operating expenses rose 12% to $850 million, reflecting our elevated R&D at $285 million or 14.2% of sales, alongside SG&A investments in commercial expansion. Adjusted operating income hit $550 million, with margins at 27.5%, up 200 basis points. Adjusted EPS was $1.55, beating consensus by $0.07.

Balance sheet remains rock-solid: $1.2 billion in cash, net debt to EBITDA at 3.2x, and free cash flow of $420 million in the quarter. We repurchased $100 million in shares and paid our quarterly dividend.

For FY2024, we're raising guidance: revenue $7.9-8.1 billion, up 17% at midpoint; adjusted EPS $6.20-6.40. Q4 revenue expected $2.05-2.10 billion, with continued mid-teens growth. Margins to expand another 100 basis points on scale. Key assumptions include stable ASPs, procedure growth at 20%, and no major supply disruptions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Elena. I'm excited to share some updates on our innovative pipeline. We recently received FDA clearance for VascuFlow XT, a groundbreaking bioresorbable drug-eluting stent system that significantly reduces restenosis rates and target lesion revascularization in PAD interventions. Building on this, our TC-7 TMVR system is advancing rapidly with strong TRILOGY trial data, and PulseGuard LA has completed IDE enrollment with superior procedure times over competitors.

In pulsed-field ablation, FARAPULSE 2.0 shows promising first-in-human results, targeting a $5 billion market. Our CardioAI platform, with 92% accuracy in restenosis prediction, nears 510(k) clearance, partnering with GE Healthcare for SaaS deployment. NeuroPulse Gen3 and RoboAssist Pro also cleared, expanding into AFib and endoscopy.

We're on track for five major launches in 2025-26, adding $2.5 billion in peak sales, supported by $1.1 billion FY R&D. Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Thornton:
Thank you, Raj. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex, could you expand on the competitive dynamics in robotics? How sustainable is the 11% share gain against Intuitive?

Alex Thornton:
Thanks, John. Our Orion Xi's rapid adoption to 11% U.S. share in soft-tissue procedures is driven by superior utilization at 85%, AI-driven EndoSense feedback, and 22% faster OR setups with FlexiArm instruments. Over 450 systems placed, with gyn and urology volumes up 35% YoY. Emerging market deals add $50 million TAM. We're challenging the monopoly through clinical evidence and partnerships, expecting continued gains into 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
Great, thanks. Elena, on R&D at 14.2% of revenue, how are you balancing the $1.1 billion FY spend with margins amid supply chain risks?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Maria. Our R&D overweight in high-ROI areas like structural heart and AI imaging is funded by strong FCF of $420 million this quarter. The 25% pipeline success rate versus industry 15% justifies it, targeting 75% gross margins on new platforms. Supply volatility for rare earths and titanium is mitigated by vertical integration and dual-sourcing, limiting impact to under 2%. Margins expanded 200 bps this quarter, and we see further leverage.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Thanks. Lisa, on ASC adoption jumping to 52%, what drives the outperformance versus hospitals, and Q4 guide?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, David. ASCs at 52% penetration, up 28% YoY, reflect the outpatient shift with 22% of our volumes now there, up from 15%. CardioGuide uptake at 61% and FlexiArm reducing turnover by 22% enable 19.2 cases/month despite smaller ORs. U.S. CMS OPPS boosts and Outcomes360 rebates tie revenue to metrics. Q4 guide 71-73% overall adoption implies $290 million consumables midpoint, ASC mix to 25%. FlexPort hub in Q1'25 targets 65% ASC pen.

Alex Thornton:
Thank you for that insight, Lisa.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, thanks. Raj, any updates on TMVR or PFA pipeline risks, especially regulatory timelines?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Emily. TC-7 TMVR PMA submits Q1 2025 post-TRILOGY's 95% success and 4.2 mmHg gradient; H2 2026 U.S. launch for $1.2B peak. FARAPULSE 2.0 first-in-human nailed 99% isolation in <20 min, zero esophageal issues; FDA mid-2025. Breakthrough designations accelerate by 6 months. China hub and EU MDR compliance derisk regionally. 24-month time-to-market and partnerships like Siemens keep us ahead.

Alex Thornton:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.
